record.provider: Beget S3 (Russia) — free egress S3 at 350 Mbit/s

free_tier.stated: No free allowance: pay-as-you-go at 0.07 RUB per 1 GB per day on used space; unlimited buckets, unlimited traffic on a 350 Mbit/s port, free GET/POST/PUT requests; stored volume is not capped.

per_object_cap.stated: 50 TB maximum object size; 5 GB maximum per upload request; at most 10000 segments in a segmented upload.
per_object_cap.notes: stated in the vendor's technical-limits list (control-panel guide)

egress.terms: FREE and generous: «Безлимитный трафик. Полоса 350 Мбит/с. Бесплатные GET/POST/PUT-запросы». Unlimited traffic, 350 Mbit/s, free GET/POST/PUT requests. A Russian price-comparison article (serverdelo.ru, prices verified 2026-10-03) independently confirms «Скачивать бесплатно можно у Beget и Рег.облака. Трафик и запросы входят в цену».

record.tooling: S3 API, HTTPS, FTP; Terraform provider (github.com/LTD-Beget/terraform-provider-beget); rclone `s3`; custom subdomain + auto SSL. Documentation and CORS supported.
record.chaining: Per-GB daily, no cap. Same rate at 5 TB and 20 TB.

limits.value: 50 TB per object; 5 GB per upload request

record.limits_note: 350 Mbit/s is the port cap, about 3.8 TB per day (derived), so serving 1 TiB per day fits with no burst; stored volume is not capped and billing is per GB per day.

identity_cost.detail: unverified: behind a sign-up; the product page does not state what registration requires (payment card, phone).

record.reliability_note: Long-running Russian shared host with 24/7 support and 99.98 % stated availability. No throttling evidence found. The commercial risk is FX: rouble pricing on a foreign card will carry the same discrimination pattern seen at Yandex.
record.confidence_note: Re-read on 2026-11-03 from vendor pages: https://beget.com/ru/cloud/storage (0.07 RUB per 1 GB per day; 350 Mbit/s port; unlimited buckets; availability 99,98%), https://beget.com/ru/kb/manual/obektnoe-hranilishche-s3-v-beget (50 TB object, 5 GB per upload request, 2000 requests per second, unlimited volume) and https://beget.com/ru/publichnaya-oferta (acceptance is by registering on the site; registration fields not listed). Registration fields stay unverified.

record.price_per_tb_month: 0.07 RUB per GB per day, 2.10 RUB per GB per month at 30 days (2,100 RUB per 1000 GB, 2,150.4 RUB per 1024 GB); egress and GET/POST/PUT requests are free; USD conversion unverified: no exchange rate was captured.
record.notes: ₽0.07 per GB per DAY (≈ ₽2.10/GB/month), billed daily on actual usage, unlimited buckets. Avail 99.98 %, three copies across servers.

dead_end.why: ₽0.07 per GB per DAY (≈ ₽2.10/GB/month), billed daily on actual usage, unlimited buckets. Avail 99.98 %, three copies across servers.

extras.price_verbatim: $26.04/TB/mo at both 5 TB and 20 TB (₽0.07/GB/day × 30 × 1024 GB × 0.012111), egress $0 and requests $0. Compare OVH One-Zone at $9.34/TB/mo with the same free-egress structure — Beget is 2.8× the price for geography.

record.binding_note: one stream is shaped, and aggregate throughput is the shaped rate times the number of streams

card.summary: A perpetual free shared-hosting account: 1 GiB SSD, one site, one FTP account and one database, unlimited domains, 10 CP of load, 25,000 file limit, PHP, Pyt...

free_tier.stated: A perpetual free shared-hosting account: 1 GiB SSD, one site, one FTP account and one database, unlimited domains, 10 CP of load, 25,000 file limit, PHP, Python, MySQL and Perl, with no advertising inserted. No technical support is provided on the free tier.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: 1 GiB of SSD with PHP and MySQL and no support is a place to park a static page or a small cron-driven script, and it composes with an external database only because the site limit is one and the database limit is one.

limits.value: The free account is registered by mobile phone and Beget's free-hosting rules require a phone number that receives the SMS code; the free tariff is documented as open to residents of Russia, Belarus, Ukraine and Kazakhstan, and the 25,000-file and 1 GiB limits bind long before any traffic limit does.

identity_cost.detail: a mobile number that receives an SMS code, restricted by country: the free-hosting rules state the applicant enters a mobile number and the SMS code, and a forum post describing the signup form states 'Beget only supports registrations via phone numbers from Russia, Belarus, Ukraine, and Kazakhstan'. The same rules page adds that Beget may request documents proving the details, which is a possible second gate. No card is stated for the free tariff, and the SMS provider is not stated
